ImageDescription.value: Humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) jumping in the air and splashing the water at Ísafjarðardjúp (Iceland). The reasons why whales practice breaching are still unknown today. Some hypotheses among others are that breaching is done in order to either communicate, court, assert dominance, warn of danger, remove parasites from the skin or play. Image set number 1 out of 5.

ImageDescription.value: Humpback whale tail (Megaptera novaeangliae) at Ísafjarðardjúp (Iceland). Each whale has unique patterns on its tail, like a fingerprint. Based on a good quality photograph of a whale tail, researchers can identify a specific individual by comparing the photo with a database of photographed whale tails. Using the GPS coordinates and the date of the photograph of each whale tail, it is possible to study the migrations carried out by each individual. Some humpback whales migrate tens of thousands of kilometres in a year. Image set number 1 out of 6.

Credit.value: Own work, from gileslaurent.com

Attribution.value: © Giles Laurent, gileslaurent.com, License CC BY-SA
